messages:
maya: quick RFC follow-up — i pushed a draft heuristic for incremental domain extraction to the repo. looking for practical concerns before we lock it.

maya: TL;DR: 1) extract hotpath slices first, 2) prefer adapter patterns over facades, 3) use a traffic mirror for 2 weeks, 4) small-canary rollout with health gates and data-ownership checklist.

dan: looked it over briefly. big question — how do we detect 'hotpath' automatically? is it latency percentiles, token churn, or call frequency?

sophie: +1 on measured heuristics. i'd vote for a composite score: p95 latency * request_rate + cache_miss_ratio. that prioritizes slices that cost us tokens and latency.

kevin: caveat: some low-call endpoints have complex state and are dangerous to move. we should mark manual-block tags for those. automation can't catch business invariants.

maya: agreed, kevin. proposal includes a manual-review flag for any candidate with >3 downstream services in dependents graph.

ravi: about the traffic mirror — do we have infra to mirror per-tenant traffic? we can do global 1% sampling today, per-tenant is harder.

infra-bot: ci:mirrors job queued for repo:redwood/runtime-refactors — will run smoke + integration once you add the MIRROR_CONFIG change.

maya: thanks — plan B: start with global mirror and a small set of pilot tenants we own. add per-tenant mirror in phase 2.

dan: rollout policy: can we use the existing switchboard to route fallback to hosted model variant if new slice regresses? want graceful degradation.

sophie: yes — switchboard already supports fallthrough routing by model-tag. we should add an automated revert trigger if error_rate > 0.5% for 10m OR p95 latency increases by 20%.

kevin: metrics we need hooked before cutover: end-to-end p50/p95, error breakdown by service, token/unit cost, and a sampling of model outputs for quality checks.

maya: adding those to the cutover checklist. also adding: contract acceptance tests, synthetic prompts, and an eval harness that runs nightly against canary traffic.

ravi: testing note: KV cache invalidation semantics will change slightly when we split. we need a backward-compat shim for cache keys for 1 month.

dan: +1 on shim. add a migration job that rehydrates new-key namespace in the background.

sophie: one more thing — telemetry. we need a per-request trace id to stitch logs across old/new paths. otherwise post-cutover debugging will be brutal.

maya: good catch. will add trace-id header requirement to all adapter shims and enforce via API linting.

kevin: timeline idea: phase 0 (2w): prepare shims, tests, mirror infra. phase 1 (3w): mirror + pilot tenants. phase 2 (2w): incremental cutovers by slice with 48h observability window each. phase 3 (ongoing): paydown and tech-debt tickets.

maya: timeline looks reasonable. we'll sync with product for tenant pick list and legal for data controls.

ravi: can someone add the MIRROR_CONFIG example to the PR? i can kick off infra changes once that's present.

maya: will do today. last item — ownership. we need a temporary oncall rota for the cutover window. volunteer? :raised_hand:

dan: can take first week of phase 1.

sophie: second week.

kevin: available for rollback support during phase 2.

maya: awesome. i'll update RFC with these action items and push a follow-up PR with the checklist, shim notes, and metric thresholds. congrats team, this is the most pragmatic path i've seen for the big untangle.

sophie: :clap: small incremental wins > big risky lifts.
